record.paper_title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem: current status and open problems
record.original_question: How do hadron masses, couplings, and related properties change inside nuclei or more generally at finite baryon density, and can partial restoration of chiral symmetry in nuclear matter be determined quantitatively from QCD itself rather than from phenomenological models? This includes determining how changes in the chiral condensate inside nuclear media modify hadronic observables and whether those modifications can be established reliably from first principles.

evidence.quote: Another open problem is the measurement of the hadron mass inside nuclei or at finite baryon density.
To understand the properties of hadrons inside the nuclear medium quantitatively, it is mandatory to use QCD.

artifact.category_tag: finite-density QCD and chiral symmetry restoration
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the SU(3) gauge theory of quarks and gluons defined by the Lagrangian \(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{QCD}} = -\tfrac{1}{4} G^a_{\mu\nu} G^{a\,\mu\nu} + \sum_f \bar\psi_f (i\gamma^\mu D_\mu - m_f)\psi_f\), at nonzero baryon chemical potential \(\mu_B\) (equivalently, in a nuclear medium of finite baryon density \(n_B > 0\)). Let \(\langle \bar q q \rangle_{n_B}\) denote the in-medium chiral (quark) condensate, and for a hadron \(H\) let \(M_H(n_B)\) and \(g_H(n_B)\) denote its in-medium mass and effective couplings, defined via the appropriate two- and three-point correlation functions of interpolating operators evaluated in the finite-density ground state of QCD.

(a) Derive, directly from QCD (e.g., via lattice QCD, QCD sum rules anchored to first-principles inputs, or a rigorous effective field theory matched to QCD), quantitative predictions for the dependence of \(M_H(n_B)\) and \(g_H(n_B)\) on \(n_B\) for representative hadrons (such as the nucleon, the \(\sigma\), \(\rho\), \(\omega\), and \(\phi\) mesons, and heavy-quarkonium states), without recourse to phenomenological hadronic models.

(b) Establish quantitatively, from QCD itself, the partial restoration of chiral symmetry in nuclear matter by computing \(\langle \bar q q \rangle_{n_B}/\langle \bar q q \rangle_{0}\) as a function of \(n_B\) and identifying the precise functional relationship between this ratio and the in-medium modifications \(M_H(n_B) - M_H(0)\) and \(g_H(n_B) - g_H(0)\).

The task is to provide such first-principles, quantitatively reliable determinations, overcoming in particular the sign problem that obstructs direct Monte Carlo simulation of lattice QCD at \(\mu_B \neq 0\).
artifact.status_search_result: This is a long-standing open problem in finite-density QCD. The sign problem prevents direct lattice Monte Carlo computation at nonzero baryon chemical potential, and current first-principles determinations of in-medium hadron properties and the in-medium chiral condensate remain limited; the problem is acknowledged as open in current reviews on finite-density lattice QCD and in-medium hadron physics.

status_evidence.title: Finite-density lattice QCD and sign problem (review)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems include measurement of hadron mass inside nuclei or at finite baryon density.
status_evidence.claim: In-medium hadron properties from QCD at finite baryon density remain an open problem due to the sign problem.
